title: MyJewl alloy price sheet v0.1
description: A versioned, cited, dated, per-alloy price per gram with an expiry. It is a COMMERCIAL input and nothing else: it turns an already-measured metal weight into a metal-content cost. It is never a manufacturing verdict, never a geometry input, never a retrieval axis, and never part of a geometry signature (settled decision 6). The committed sheet ships 'undeclared' and refuses all of its own values, exactly as the shop-profile template does -- MyJewl does not invent market data.

status.description: 'undeclared' means no price in this sheet may be used, regardless of any individual entry's status. This is the state the repository ships in.

currency.description: ISO 4217, one currency per sheet. A sheet mixing currencies would let a quote add USD to EUR, so the loader takes the sheet's currency as the currency of every entry in it.

declared_by.description: Who takes responsibility for these numbers. A price with no owner is a rumour.

validity.description: Metal prices move daily. A sheet with no expiry is a sheet that quietly goes stale, and a stale price is worse than no price because it looks live.

prices.description: Keyed by the exact alloy token from fast_mvp.typed_inputs (14k_yellow, 14k_white, 14k_rose, 18k_yellow, 18k_white, 18k_rose, pt950). There is deliberately NO wildcard: pt950 and 14k_yellow differ by roughly an order of magnitude per gram, so a price that spans alloys is always wrong for at least one of them. An absent alloy is priced by nothing.

certifies_manufacturing.description: Structurally false. A cost moves no geometry gate.

affects_geometry.description: Structurally false. Metal is a cost/appearance overlay (settled decision 6): two rings identical except for alloy are the same geometry and must retrieve, validate, and hash identically.

price_entry.description: One alloy's price per gram, with the provenance that makes it usable. An entry that does not state WHAT the price covers is refused, the same way the shop profile refuses a minimum with no unsupported-span qualifier: an unqualified number cannot be checked by the person reading it.

as_of.description: The date this price was true. Not the date it was typed in.

expires_on.description: Per-entry expiry. Alloys move independently, so a sheet-level expiry alone is not enough.

price_basis.description: What the number covers. 'unknown' is refused: a reader cannot tell whether it already includes casting loss and refining, and the difference is material.

source.description: Where the number came from: a refiner's quote, a supplier price list, a dated market reference, or 'undeclared_placeholder'.
